parts.text: Differentiate between the following sets of concepts.
Conceptualization and operationalization
Reliability and validity
Both pure and social sciences follow a research process based on the scientific method. Draw and describe a basic scientific method process framework.
The eventual outcome of a research process is a research report. Briefly describe what goes into each part of a research report's outline.

items.text: Variables must clearly be defined to ensure accurate measurement.

parts.text: Distinguish between the following types of variables.
Independent and dependent variables
Control and intervening variables
Discuss three types of relationships among variables.

items.text: Ekai's research topic states: "The effectiveness of fear appeals from the Kenya Ministry of Health daily Covid-19 briefings." He develops his argument from media reports portraying that Kenyans seem not to be quite keen in heeding the Ministry of Health messages about this disease. The researcher intends to collect data from the general public. The research has three objectives: (1) to find out whether Kenyans can identify the fear appeals in the messages; (2) to explore the success of the fear appeal messages; (3) to explore the failures of the fear appeal messages. On the basis of the topic and objectives:

parts.text: Identify five ethical issues Ekai is likely to encounter.
Propose a remedy for each of the ethical issues.
State two popular types of questions used in a research questionnaire.
Select one of the types of questions in (a) above and:
Justify three advantages.
Justify three disadvantages.
Provide six guidelines for questionnaire question construction.

items.text: Sampling methods can be classified into two broad categories: probability and non-probability methods.

parts.text: Explain four probability sampling techniques.
Describe the procedure used when sampling using the following techniques.
Snowball sampling
Purposive sampling
